solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rumour president once put before us?

parts.note: George W. Bush, a former US president
the Daily Telegraph is the newspaper put before us solvers, carrying this very puzzle

explanation.surface: A rumour about some former president that has been placed in front of us.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: the paper put before you is the Telegraph, where this puzzle appears.
explanation.definitionFit: The bush telegraph is an informal grapevine by which gossip spreads, so it stands for rumour itself.

clue.text: Slob with nausea agog about fare from Italy

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so the letters of these three words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A lazy person, queasy yet eager, hovering around some Italian food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the anagram signal: SLOB, NAUSEA and AGOG are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: This large cured sausage from the city of Bologna is food originating in Italy, hence Italian fare.

clue.text: Means of detecting boy raised in crime

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a piece within the word lifts it from the bottom to the top

parts.note: arson is the crime of setting fires
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Some method of catching a lad who grew up surrounded by criminality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised in' moves SON from the foot of ARSON to its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonar finds submarines and shoals by sound echoes, a technique for detecting things underwater.

clue.text: Provider of change following childish fall-out?

definitions.text: Provider of change following childish fall-out?

parts.words: Provider of change following childish fall-out?
parts.note: a child's milk teeth falling out is rewarded with coins left under the pillow

explanation.surface: Someone who brings about change after a petty quarrel between children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall-out' looks like a row; it is teeth literally falling out, and 'change' is loose coins.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery legend swaps a lost milk tooth under the pillow for a small coin, giving loose money to children.

clue.text: Love copper to be hugged by bit of fluff in print

indicators.note: being hugged means being held within the arms of the next piece

parts.note: lint is fluff from fabric
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A romantic policeman embraced by an attractive young woman, caught on film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of fluff' suggests a young woman, but it is lint.
explanation.definitionFit: A linocut is a picture printed from a carved block of linoleum, so it is a kind of print.

clue.text: Atlases, say, complete welcome surprise

parts.note: Atlas was a Titan of Greek myth, so figures like him are deities
to complete something is to end it

explanation.surface: Map books that finally arrive whole come as a pleasant shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Atlases' suggests books of maps; here they are mythological Titans like Atlas.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is an unexpected stroke of good fortune, as if sent from heaven.

clue.text: Top banana ultimately wanting large muscles for audition

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word banana
for audition means as heard by a listener, so the spelling follows the spoken word

parts.note: pecs are the large chest muscles, the pectorals

explanation.surface: A top banana in show business who wants to be muscle-bound before trying out for a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top banana' reads as a phrase for a star performer; 'Top' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or peak of something, its very top.

clue.text: Dislike consuming iodine, boring served up as mineral

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing up the following pieces inside

parts.note: to dislike strongly is to hate

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: tame means dull or boring
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes iodine and finds a dull dish served up as a mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'served up' means written upwards, so the reversal reads bottom to top; 'consuming' wraps the dislike around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Haematite is the principal ore of iron, a reddish iron oxide mineral.

clue.text: This could be viewed as a plus sign for part of the UK

definitions.text: This could be viewed as a plus sign for part of the UK

parts.words: This could be viewed as a plus sign for part of the UK
parts.note: a plus sign is a cross, and England's flag shows a red upright cross on white

explanation.surface: Something viewed as a positive sign for one region of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plus sign' reads as a good omen; taken literally it is a cross shape, the flag of England, which is part of the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: England's patron saint gives his name to the red cross on a white field that forms the English flag.

clue.text: Secure work after rejection, keeping fine with no sleep

parts.note: to land something is to secure it

indicators.note: keeping means holding the following pieces inside
rejected means thrown back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: do means work, as in do a job
F is short for fine on pencil grades

explanation.surface: Landing a job after being turned down, but keeping fine with no rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after rejection' reads the word for work backwards to give OD; 'keeping' then holds F and NO between its letters. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical land east of Eden became a jocular name for the state of slumber.

clue.text: Chuck out English cape in black

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: jet is a deep black
C abbreviates cape on maps

explanation.surface: Throwing out an Englishman in a black cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject is to throw someone forcibly out, which is what chucking out does.

clue.text: Bale possibly abandoned by eastern courtyard

indicators.note: abandoned by means losing the next piece from the word

parts.note: Gareth Bale is a Welsh footballer, so Gareth is one example of a Bale

explanation.surface: A hay bale left lying in a courtyard by someone from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bale' looks like hay, but it is footballer Gareth Bale; 'possibly' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A garth is an old word for an enclosed yard or the garden in a cloister.

clue.text: On reflection, what's hidden by undercover status on street?

indicators.note: on reflection means as seen in a mirror, read backwards
hidden by means the letters sit inside the word undercover

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, what does an undercover agent conceal about standing among the criminals?
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden by' finds DERC within 'undercover' and 'On reflection' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Street cred is standing or credibility among fashionable or tough young people.

clue.text: Beware getting caught by hail

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
ave is the Latin greeting hail

explanation.surface: A warning against being caught out in a hailstorm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hail' looks like the weather; it is the Latin greeting. CAVE is Latin for beware, the schoolboy's warning that a master is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin this is the imperative warning to take care, once used at English public schools.

clue.text: Novel concerned with river turning blue

parts.note: in means involved or concerned with

indicators.note: turning means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: the Avon is an English river
blue is the colour of the Conservatives, so a blue is a Tory

explanation.surface: A novel about a river that turns blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book but is the adjective; 'blue' is a Conservative, a Tory, from the party colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something new and original, introducing fresh ideas.

clue.text: Stop by snake and put it on road

indicators.note: by means next to, so the snake sits beside the word for stop

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
halt means stop

explanation.surface: A driver halts beside a snake and then sets off along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the definition is the answer itself: to asphalt is to lay this surface on a road.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, it means to surface a road with the tarry paving material, laying it down.

clue.text: Smashed CIA, partly struggling

indicators.note: struggling suggests a disordered state, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: The CIA, somewhat floundering, has been crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashed' looks like broken; it is slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for very drunk, so intoxicated as to be unable to move properly.

clue.text: Smaller daughter wants more Sooty?

parts.note: inkier means blacker, more like soot

explanation.surface: A younger daughter asks for more of the children's puppet Sooty.
explanation.walkthrough: Sooty is a yellow bear glove puppet on British children's TV; the capital hides the adjective sooty.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinky is British for small and neat, so its comparative means more compact or littler.

clue.text: Stewards et al in carriage were boasting

parts.note: one's carriage or bearing is one's air
crew is a past tense of crow, to boast

explanation.surface: Railway stewards and staff in a carriage were bragging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carriage' looks like a railway coach; it is bearing, or air. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The staff who work on an aircraft, cabin attendants among them, make up its flight team.

clue.text: Bug one father about being subservient to wife

indicators.note: in a down clue, being subservient means placed below, so these pieces come after

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pater is Latin, and old schoolboy slang, for father

explanation.surface: Bothering a father who lives under his wife's thumb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns PATER into RETAP; 'being subservient to' puts I and that below W.
explanation.definitionFit: A bug is a hidden listening device, and a phone wiretap is a covert eavesdropping device.

clue.text: My weight's massive after vacation

parts.note: a stone is a unit of weight, 14 pounds

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outside letters of massive remain

explanation.surface: Someone back from holiday complains of having gained a lot of weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive but is an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated British exclamations of mild surprise or astonishment.

clue.text: Leak unfinished instruction to read elsewhere?

parts.note: a cross-reference in a book directs the reader to another page, here without its page number

explanation.surface: A leak from an incomplete directive to read something else.
explanation.walkthrough: Split three and four, the answer is a book's cross-reference, missing the page number that would finish it.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is liquid slowly oozing through, as from a leak.

clue.text: Identity of family held back after husband goes missing

indicators.note: held back means pulled backwards, reversing the word
goes missing means the letter is removed

parts.note: one's flesh and blood is one's family, so flesh stands for it

explanation.surface: A family's identity being concealed once the husband disappears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes missing' drops H from FLESH, and 'held back' reverses the FLES that remains.
explanation.definitionFit: One's self is one's essential being, the individual identity that makes one who one is.

clue.text: Encourage doctor to cast off son

indicators.note: cast off means discarded, so the letters are removed

parts.note: a surgeon is a medical doctor
spelt as written

explanation.surface: Urging a doctor to disown his son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cast off' removes S, O and N, scattered through SURGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone is to press or encourage them strongly to act.

clue.text: Old person at peace regularly embracing unknown

indicators.note: embracing means holding the next piece in its arms

parts.note: z is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word peace

explanation.surface: An elderly person at peace, regularly holding someone unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes E and C from peace; with AT they make ATEC, around Z.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztecs were the people of a Mexican empire that fell in the 16th century, an ancient civilisation.

clue.text: Gasquet's last to wear hat in championship

indicators.note: to wear means to be clad in, so the hat surrounds the letter

parts.note: tile is slang for a hat

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the tennis player's surname

explanation.surface: French tennis player Richard Gasquet finally donning a hat to win a championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gasquet's last' is T, the final letter of the player's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is a sporting championship, as in winning a world title.

clue.text: Film industry in LA finally finds flapper who can speak

indicators.note: finally picks the final letters of each of these four words

explanation.surface: Hollywood's film industry finds a fast-talking 1920s flapper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flapper' suggests a 1920s girl; it is a bird, flapping its wings, that mimics speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The myna is a starling of Asia renowned for imitating human talk, a winged mimic.

clue.text: Eviscerate extremely smelly game

parts.note: to gut is to remove the innards

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme, outside letters of smelly

explanation.surface: Disembowelling some foul-smelling game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like birds for the table; it is the adjective meaning plucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Game means willing and plucky, and gutsy means brave and spirited.

clue.text: Air foul footwear after short time

indicators.note: after means the anagram comes later than the letter for time

parts.note: T abbreviates time

indicators.note: foul means corrupted, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Smelly shoes being aired after a little while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' looks like ventilating the shoes; it is a tune, the song from No, No, Nanette.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune, and this is a well-known popular song from a 1920s musical.

clue.text: Married men touring that city meeting escorts in avenue abroad

indicators.note: touring means going around the next piece

parts.note: chaps are men
Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England
to see someone home is to escort them

explanation.surface: Husbands visiting a city meet hired companions on a foreign boulevard.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a small English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Champs-Elysees is the grand Paris avenue running to the Arc de Triomphe.
